meta.title: SLATE research gaps: hotel early check-in / late check-out requests; uninsured walk-in prices (Toronto); NHS Scotland overseas-visitor charging and costs; GP same/next-day access and ED substitution
meta.method: WebSearch, WebFetch and curl. PDFs and .xlsx workbooks were downloaded and parsed locally (a ToUnicode-aware PDF text extractor and an xlsx sheet dumper written for this pass), so figures marked 'page' from a PDF/xlsx were read in the document itself. Nothing is invented; where nothing is published the value is null with the reason.

verificationLevels.page: Read on the cited page or in the cited document itself.
verificationLevels.search-summary: Taken only from the search engine's summary of the cited page; the page itself was not read (usually HTTP 403). Re-check before shipping as a hard figure.
verificationLevels.derived: Arithmetic on figures read on the page; the formula is given.

cautions: A WebFetch summary of Scottish CEL 09 (2010) claimed the text says overseas visitors 'should be charged the full cost'. The PDF was then parsed locally and contains no such sentence; it says Boards should 'recover the cost of NHS treatment'. The fetcher's quote was a fabrication and is not used.
Third-party figures seen in search summaries but NOT traced to the hotel (Travelodge IE EUR 10, The Dean EUR 20, Travelodge UK GBP 10, Accor Gold 2pm) are listed as notes only, never as values.

hotelRequests.summary: Of SLATE's 28 hotels, the hotel's own site publishes a hard early/late price for only a few: Hotel Catedral (late check-out to 19:00, MXN 553 flat), Freehand LA (late to 15:00 at 50% of the nightly rate; early from 12:00 for an unstated 'small fee'), The Beverly Hills Hotel (late to 16:00 at 50% of best available rate; search-summary), Omni New Haven (late from USD 50; search-summary), The Hoxton Holborn (GBP 10/hour to 16:00; search-summary; free 'Flexy Time' for direct bookings 72h ahead, page). Every other hotel says 'subject to availability' and either 'additional fees may apply' with no amount, or nothing. No hotel guarantees early check-in except by booking the previous night (Beverly Hills Hotel, Four Seasons Toronto and Mexico City say so).

grantRateStatistic.why: No published industry survey (J.D. Power NAGSI, Skift, STR, Oracle Hospitality, chain disclosures) reports the share of early check-in or late check-out requests that hotels grant. Searches on 2026-10-01/02 found only uncited blog figures ('68% of hotels more likely to grant...', '30% of guests request late check-out', '75% of hotels offer late check-out') attributed vaguely to 'Hotel News Resource' or similar, with no methodology; these must not be used. research-sweep4.json reached the same conclusion on 2026-09-30.

regulation.name: The National Health Service (Charges to Overseas Visitors) (Scotland) Regulations 1989 (SI 1989/364), as amended

latestAmendment.name: The National Health Service (Charges to Overseas Visitors) (Scotland) Amendment Regulations 2025 (SSI 2025/280)
latestAmendment.effect: Inserts regulation 4D exempting people evacuated from Gaza for treatment (and accompanying persons), with charges from 2025-09-15 not made or repaid.

aAndE.text: Reg. 3(a): no charge for services at a hospital accident and emergency department or casualty department. NHS inform: 'Emergency treatment is free of charge in: accident and emergency (A&E); a casualty department; NHS walk-in centres that provide services like those in A&E.'

gp.text: Reg. 3(b): no charge for services provided otherwise than at or by a hospital (except an oral health assessment, dental examination, eye examination or sight test), which covers GP care. NHS inform: 'If you are registered as a temporary resident, you will not need to pay to see the GP.'

freeServices.otherExemptServices: Reg. 3: family planning; Schedule 1 notifiable diseases; STI clinics; detention under the Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003; treatment required by a community payback order.

charged.text: NHS inform: 'You may be charged if you're admitted to hospital as an inpatient or if you're registered as an outpatient.' NHS Forth Valley: 'All treatment provided which is deemed immediately necessary may be chargeable. This includes Inpatient, Outpatient and Daycase treatment.'

chargeRate.value: the cost of treatment (100%); no uplift is published for Scotland
chargeRate.text: Scottish Government CEL 09 (2010), 9 April 2010, para 12: 'The Scottish Government expects NHS Boards to take all reasonable steps to recover the cost of NHS treatment from those overseas visitors who are liable to charges under the Regulations.' Neither the 1989 Regulations (reg. 2 says Boards 'make and recover... charges' with no formula) nor NHS inform nor NHS Forth Valley publishes a percentage uplift.

england150.text: The 150% of the NHS national tariff applies in England (NHS (Charges to Overseas Visitors) Regulations 2015 as amended in 2017). It is not Scottish law.

chargeRate.note: Treat the 100% as 'cost recovery, no published uplift', not as a stated percentage. Boards do not publish their invoice tariffs. The natural cost basis is the PHS Scottish Health Service Costs figures below.

costBook.publisher: Public Health Scotland, Scottish Health Service Costs, year ended 31 March 2024 (published 25 Feb 2025; NHS Tayside data revised 8 Apr 2025). NHS Borders is excluded from the Scotland totals.
costBook.whyNot2024_25: The 2024/25 release (11 Aug 2026) published only summary tables (R100T, R086, R910, R920, R921), with no specialty cost-per-case workbooks, because NHS boards were moving to PLICS. 2023/24 is the latest year with per-case figures.

commonwealthFund2023.survey: Commonwealth Fund 2023 International Health Policy Survey (adults 18+, 10 countries; fieldwork 2023). It is the latest general-adult wave; the 2024 wave surveyed adults 65+ only.

sameOrNextDayHeadline.definition: Last time sick or needed care, got an appointment the same or next day. Base excludes 'did not need an appointment', 'not sure', 'declined', and 'never able to get one'.

q9RawDistribution.question: Q9: Last time you were sick or needed to see a doctor or a nurse, how quickly could you get an appointment? (excludes ED visits)

edCouldHaveBeenTreatedByRegularDoctor.question: Q20: The last time you went to the hospital emergency department, was it for a condition that you thought could have been treated by the doctors or staff at the place where you usually get medical care... if they had been available?
edCouldHaveBeenTreatedByRegularDoctor.base: Respondents who used an ED in the past 2 years (CIHI: those with a regular provider who visited the ED)

corroboration.text: CIHI: 'Of Canadians who have a primary care provider and visited the ED, 2 in 5 reported that their last ED visit could have been managed at their usual place of care'; '75% of Canadians who reported that their ED visit could have been managed elsewhere also reported not being able to get a same- or next-day appointment.'

ireland.commonwealthFund: Ireland is not in the Commonwealth Fund survey.

officialStatistic.why: No ICGP, Healthy Ireland or CSO publication of GP wait days or same-day access was found. The CSO Irish Health Survey and Healthy Ireland report GP visit rates and cost barriers, not waits.

poll.survey: Ipsos B&A poll for the Irish Examiner, 'Rural Ireland Thinks'
poll.note: Sample size not stated in the article. The same 54% was reported in the previous wave. Respondents are rural, so it does not measure Dublin; use it only as an indication for Ireland.

imssUmfWait.survey: IMSS Encuesta de Calidad (ENCAL 2025), first level of care (Unidades de Medicina Familiar), executive report; fieldwork October–November 2025 in 262 first-level units; adult patients interviewed at the end of their visit
imssUmfWait.text: '29 días promedio entre solicitud de cita y atención'; '76% de usuarios espera 2 semanas o más'; '87% de los usuarios que acuden con cita reporta estar satisfecho o muy satisfecho con la espera en la unidad'; 'cada 10 minutos adicionales de espera reducen la probabilidad de alta satisfacción en 4.5%'.

ensanut.why: ENSANUT national reports do not publish days-to-appointment at an IMSS UMF. The state-level ENSANUT Continua 2022 Guanajuato report gives an average waiting-room wait of 54.6 minutes and consultation of 37.3 minutes, across all institutions in that state.

olderFigure.text: Average wait for a consultation at IMSS, from CIEP 'Sistema Universal de Salud: Retos de cobertura y financiamiento', as reported by Saludiario 2022-03-05.
olderFigure.note: Secondary report. The CIEP data year is not stated. ENCAL 2025 supersedes it.
